subject: Request: temporary quota & fairness exemption for pilot go-live (Aperture Health)
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aperturehealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Josh Santana <j.santana@aperturehealth.com>, Aperture Health Procurement <procurement@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 08:24:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot go-live next week — request for temporary quota/fairness exception

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Our pilot with the patient triage assistant is scheduled to go live next Tuesday (2/17). Based on updated traffic forecasts the pilot will hit sustained bursts (~2x our original forecast) for the first 72 hours as clinical teams ramp usage.

We understand Redwood has fairness policies and burst quotas, but given the short, time-boxed ramp we wanted to ask whether Aperture can get a temporary increase to our per-minute rate cap and a reduced fairness weighting so our pilot traffic isn’t throttled during business hours.

Readouts we need to sign off on:
- Temporary per-minute token cap increase to 3x (2/17–2/19)
- Bypass of fairness de-prioritization for the pilot app during 8am–6pm ET
- Clear rollback at end of 2/19 and monitoring/reporting during the window

Attached is our revised traffic forecast (aperture_pilot_traffic_forecast.xlsx). If this requires an SLA exception or exec signoff, please let us know what you need. We’re flexible on any mitigation you need (e.g., circuit breakers, throttling to X% after spike).

Appreciate the help — we want a smooth launch and don’t want to impact other customers.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Digital Channels
Aperture Health

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live next week — request for temporary quota/fairness exception

Hi Maria,

Thanks for the forecast and the clear ask — that helps. I’ve looped in Rachel (account lead) and our infra lead (Vivek) to evaluate feasibility and risk. We can often accommodate short, targeted exceptions but need an operational plan and rollback guardrails.

Action items from our side:
- Internal assessment of capacity impact and fairness trade-offs (Vivek)
- Written temporary terms (duration, exact caps, monitoring, rollback) — I’ll draft 
- DocuSign/approval path for your procurement team if required

Rachel — can you confirm Aperture’s SLA tier and who signs for procurement? Maria included procurement on the thread.

I’ll aim to get a proposed terms PDF by EOD tomorrow (2/10).

Best,
Naomi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 10:07:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot go-live next week — request for temporary quota/fairness exception

Folks — forwarding Aperture’s ask. Key points: 3x per-minute token cap for 72 hours and exemption from fairness de-prioritization during business hours. They are offering to accept circuit breakers if needed.

Please reply with:
- Feasibility (yes/no) and approximate risk to other customers
- Suggested mitigation (rate limiting tiers, circuit breaker thresholds, rolling window limits)
- Monitoring & escalation plan (dashboard/alerting)

Vivek — can engineering support a temporary profile that relaxes fairness and increases per-minute token cap per their ask? If so, what guardrails do we require?

Thanks,
Naomi

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot go-live next week — request for temporary quota/fairness exception

Naomi / team,

Short answer: feasible with constraints. Longer: our fairness scheduler enforces weighted queuing to prevent noisy neighbors. We can deploy a temporary "pilot profile" that:
- Increases per-minute token cap for Aperture to 3x (as requested) for a configured 72-hour window
- Applies a temporary fairness weight bump so Aperture requests are processed ahead of lower-priority jobs during 08:00–18:00 ET
- Adds a live circuit breaker that drops new requests if CPU or GPU load exceeds 85% cluster capacity for more than 2 minutes

Mitigations & notes:
- We will rate-limit by token/sec and have a soft + hard cap: soft cap = 3x (throttle to 50% beyond that for 60s), hard cap = 5x (reject) — gives breathing room but prevents runaway usage
- Telemetry: create a dedicated dashboard and set pager on sustained error rate/latency degradation (>20% P95 increase or >2% error rate increase across region)
- Rollback: automatic revert at 2026-02-19T00:00:00Z + manual kill switch for CS/eng if any cross-customer SLA regressions observed
- Implementation: needs a config change and a short maintenance deployment window (we can do a config push at 02/16 22:00–22:15 ET).

Attachments: capacity_plan.pdf (draft), redwood_temp_quota_terms.pdf (wording we can share with procurement).

Risk: low-medium; the fairness change has the potential to slightly increase latency for lower-priority customers during the window, but the circuit breaker keeps system risk bounded. We should require Aperture to agree to explicit rollback and alerting.

If approved, I’ll implement the profile and coordinate with SRE on dashboards.

-Vivek
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aperturehealth.com>, Josh Santana <j.santana@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aperture Health Procurement <procurement@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Proposed temporary quota/fairness terms for Aperture pilot (2/17–2/19)

Hi Maria / Josh,

Thanks for the quick sync. Per internal review, Redwood can support a time-boxed exception under the following terms (attached PDF: redwood_temp_quota_terms.pdf):

Summary of proposal
- Window: 2026-02-17 00:00 UTC through 2026-02-20 00:00 UTC (72 hours)
- Per-minute token cap: increased to 3x baseline (soft throttle at 3x, hard reject at 5x)
- Fairness: apply elevated processing weight for Aperture’s pilot requests between 08:00–18:00 ET during the window
- Circuit breaker: automatic disable if cluster GPU/CPU >85% for >2 minutes; manual kill available to Redwood CS/Eng
- Monitoring: dedicated dashboard, hourly PDF summary to Aperture contacts during the window
- Rollback: automatic at window end + immediate rollback on cross-customer SLA regressions

Operational requirements from Aperture
- Sign and return the temporary exception terms (DocuSign link below)
- Provide a 24/7 on-call contact for the pilot window
- Agree to agreed-upon traffic shaping if we hit circuit breaker

If this works, we’ll schedule the configuration push and create the dashboard. Rachel — can you confirm procurement lead for DocuSign?

DocuSign: https://docusign.redwood/sign/D-2026-AP-1143-temp-terms
Drive: https://drive.redwood/capacity_plan/aperture_pilot

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
